name: University of Connecticut

financial.note: Borrowed $582 million in March 2026, the largest amount ever borrowed in this program's 30 year history, to pay for academic and research buildings

demand.note: About 66,300 students applied for Fall 2025, the highest number ever

housing.note: 2,253 students were offered a spot on the waitlist, 979 accepted it, and 550 got in; 96 percent of first year students live on campus

confirmation.note: The bond sale is already closed, not just planned

flagNote: Record numbers of students are applying, and the school just closed the largest construction loan in its history.

admissions.text: About 66,300 students applied to enter in Fall 2025, the most ever. UConn ranks 32nd among public universities nationally, according to US News.
admissions.source: UConn's own report to its bondholders

financial.text: UConn closed a $582 million bond sale on March 24, 2026, the largest in the 30 year history of its UConn 2000 building program. The money pays for academic and research buildings, library upgrades, and infrastructure at both the Storrs campus and UConn Health, and also refinances older debt from 2015 and 2016.
financial.source: Connecticut State Treasurer's office and the Hartford Business Journal

housing.text: 2,253 students were offered a waitlist spot, 979 accepted, and 550 were admitted from the waitlist. 96 percent of first year students and 64 percent of all undergraduates live in college housing.
housing.source: UConn's own reported enrollment data for 2023 to 2024

name: Northeastern University

financial.note: A $378.5 million science building loan and a separate new dorm are both being built at the same time

demand.note: Known for being hard to get into, but we did not re-check current numbers

housing.note: The school did not report waitlist numbers this year; 99 percent of first year students live on campus

confirmation.note: Two separate, named, funded projects, both already underway

flagNote: Two large construction projects are happening at the same time, one academic building and one dorm.

admissions.text: Around 15,000 undergraduate and graduate students. The school is known for being hard to get into and having strong demand, though we did not independently re-check current figures this time.

financial.text: Northeastern took out a $378.5 million tax exempt loan through MassDevelopment around September 2025 to build a 340,000 square foot science and engineering building in the Fenway neighborhood. Separately, the school broke ground in February 2026 on a 23 story, 1,200 bed dorm, built with private partners American Campus Communities and Blackstone.
financial.source: Worcester Business Journal and Boston Real Estate Times

housing.text: The school left the waitlist fields blank this reporting year. 99 percent of first year students and 57 percent of all undergraduates live in college housing.
housing.source: Northeastern's own reported enrollment data for 2024 to 2025

name: Dartmouth College

financial.note: Borrowed over $450 million just for housing construction, and holds the highest possible credit rating

demand.note: Only accepted 5.84 percent of 28,863 applicants, near a record low

housing.note: 2,497 students offered a waitlist spot; 100 percent of first years and 85 percent of all undergraduates live on campus

confirmation.note: The construction loan is active and confirmed, not just proposed

flagNote: Confirmed live opportunity: over $450 million borrowed for construction, a record-low acceptance rate, and real waitlist demand.

admissions.text: For the class entering in 2026, Dartmouth admitted 1,687 out of 28,863 applicants, a 5.84 percent acceptance rate. The school reports 4,715 undergraduates total, and 2,497 students were offered a waitlist spot this year, though it has not published how many accepted.
admissions.source: AdmissionSight and commondatasets.fyi, both citing Dartmouth's own reported enrollment data for the 2025 to 2026 school year

financial.text: Dartmouth borrowed more than $450 million in 2025 for campus construction, including new housing. Its credit rating was raised to AAA, the highest grade a rating agency gives, back in 2024.
financial.source: The Dartmouth student newspaper and S&P Global Ratings
financial.asOf: Bond issue: August 2025. Credit rating: April 2024

housing.text: 2,497 students were offered a waitlist spot this year, though the school has not published how many accepted or were admitted from it. 100 percent of first year students, 85 percent of all undergraduates, and 80 percent of upperclassmen live in college housing.
housing.source: Dartmouth's own reported enrollment data for the 2025 to 2026 school year

name: Wesleyan University

financial.note: A $130 million loan is paying for a new science building opening in Fall 2026

demand.note: We did not independently check current admissions numbers

housing.note: 100 percent of first years and 99 percent of all undergraduates live on campus, near full capacity

confirmation.note: The building is already under construction, confirmed

flagNote: A large, loan funded science building is already under construction and set to open in 2026.

admissions.text: We did not independently re-check current admissions numbers this time. This school was flagged because a public campus review mentioned active science building construction, which we then confirmed separately.

financial.text: A $255 million new science building is under construction and set to open in Fall 2026, with $130 million of it paid for through a loan, according to the Hartford Business Journal. The school is also in the middle of renovating its Public Affairs Center and building an integrated arts lab.
financial.source: Hartford Business Journal and Tradeline Inc.

housing.text: 2,754 students were offered a waitlist spot, 1,557 accepted, and 81 were admitted from it. 100 percent of first year students and 99 percent of all undergraduates live in college housing. The 2022 to 2023 school year is the most recent report we could find publicly; a newer one may exist.
housing.source: Wesleyan's own reported enrollment data for 2022 to 2023

name: Trinity College

financial.note: $42 million and $13 million in loans, mostly for renovation and refinancing, not new buildings

demand.note: Deposits from incoming students are up more than 25 percent from last year, the strongest in five years

housing.note: 2,468 students offered a waitlist spot, 1,387 accepted, 19 admitted; 100 percent of first years and 82 percent of all undergraduates live on campus

confirmation.note: The loans are approved and issued, and part of the school's capital budget

flagNote: Real construction loans landed in the same year as a real jump in incoming student deposits.

admissions.text: Deposits from the incoming class entering in 2026 are up more than 25 percent from last year, the strongest year for keeping admitted students in more than five years, according to the college's own announcement.

financial.text: Connecticut's higher education finance authority approved a $42 million bond for Trinity in December 2025, with about $10 million going toward campus renovation and the rest refinancing older debt. Moody's confirmed the school's A2 credit rating with a stable outlook in February 2026. A separate $13 million bond from December 2025 is paying for first year dorm renovations and HVAC upgrades.
financial.source: Hartford Business Journal, the Trinity Tripod student newspaper, and Trinity College's own news releases

housing.text: 2,468 students were offered a waitlist spot, 1,387 accepted, and 19 were admitted from it. 100 percent of first year students and 82 percent of all undergraduates live in college housing.
housing.source: Trinity College's own reported enrollment data for 2025 to 2026

name: UMass Amherst

financial.note: Signed a housing developer deal but has not disclosed the dollar amount; a separate state loan bill is still pending

demand.note: We did not independently check current admissions numbers

housing.note: 11,100 students offered a waitlist spot, 7,261 accepted, 2,349 admitted; 97 percent of first years and 58 percent of all undergraduates live on campus

confirmation.note: A developer is picked, but the project size and dollar amount are not public yet, and the state loan bill has not passed

flagNote: A real housing deal is signed and tied to a statewide construction loan bill in progress, but neither has a confirmed dollar figure yet.

admissions.text: We did not independently re-check current admissions numbers this round.

financial.text: UMass Amherst picked American Campus Communities, owned by Blackstone, to run a full campus housing overhaul announced in May 2026. It is a long, phased plan expected to take 10 to 15 years. Separately, Massachusetts is considering the BRIGHT Act, a state construction loan bill worth more than $2.5 billion. The House passed it in November 2025, and it is still waiting on the Senate.
financial.source: Daily Hampshire Gazette and UMass Amherst's own news releases

housing.text: 11,100 students were offered a waitlist spot, 7,261 accepted, and 2,349 were admitted from it. 97 percent of first year students and 58 percent of all undergraduates live in college housing.
housing.source: UMass Amherst's own reported enrollment data for 2025 to 2026

name: Bridgewater State University

financial.note: Named in a pending state loan bill, but no project specific to this school is confirmed yet

demand.note: The school's own report says enrollment is growing, but we did not independently check the exact numbers

housing.note: The school does not run a waitlist; only 36 percent of first years and 17 percent of all undergraduates live on campus, showing low pressure

confirmation.note: The loan bill has only passed one part of the state legislature so far, not yet law

flagNote: The closest direct tie to Massachusetts's pending construction loan bill of any school checked, but nothing specific to this campus is confirmed yet.

admissions.text: The school's own financial report says enrollment growth is a factor in its revenue for the year ending June 2025, though we did not independently check the exact numbers.
admissions.source: Bridgewater State's own annual financial report

financial.text: Bridgewater State is directly named in the governor's announcement of the BRIGHT Act, a statewide construction loan bill that passed the House in November 2025. The school holds an Aa3 credit rating from Moody's. In the year ending June 2025, state funding improved the Maxwell Library and renovated Burnell Hall.
financial.source: Bridgewater State's own annual financial report and Barr & Barr construction company

housing.text: The school reports that it does not run a waitlist at all. 36 percent of first year students and 17 percent of all undergraduates live in college housing, the most recent year we could find published.
housing.source: Bridgewater State's own reported enrollment data for 2020 to 2021, the most recent edition we could find

name: University of Maine

financial.note: A $25 million loan for electrical work is active, but most current construction is paid for by donors, not loans

demand.note: Credit hours are down 4 percent from budget, and fewer out of state students are enrolling

housing.note: The waitlist numbers in the source document were not readable; 89.8 percent of first years and 38 percent of all undergraduates live on campus

confirmation.note: One loan is confirmed, but it is for electrical infrastructure, not a building

flagNote: A real, well documented need, but most current construction is paid for by donors rather than loans, which makes it a weaker fit for a loan timing pitch.

admissions.text: The university president's 2026 address said graduate enrollment is up, but credit hours taught are down 4 percent from budget, and fewer out of state students are enrolling.
admissions.source: The Maine Campus student newspaper, reporting the president's State of the University address

financial.text: Estimates for the school's total deferred maintenance backlog range widely across sources, from $1.1 billion to $1.8 billion, depending on the year and what is counted, so we are not treating any single number as fact. The school does have one active $25 million, 30 year loan for electrical infrastructure work. About 10 capital projects are finishing in 2026, and several of those are paid for by donors rather than loans.
financial.source: University of Maine's own facilities office, its governing board's meeting minutes, and the Bangor Daily News

housing.text: The waitlist section of the source document exists, but the numbers in it were not legible enough to read this time. 89.8 percent of first year students and 38 percent of all undergraduates live in college housing.
housing.source: University of Maine's own reported enrollment data for 2022 to 2023, the most recent edition we could open (newer editions exist but were not accessible)

name: University of Hartford

financial.note: Credit rating was downgraded below investment grade, the school broke a loan agreement, and it is running an operating deficit

demand.note: We did not find any sign that enrollment is growing

housing.note: This school has not published enrollment data of this kind anywhere we could find

confirmation.note: Only past projects exist, nothing new is currently planned

flagNote: This is a real signal, but a warning one. This school is in financial trouble, not a construction spending opportunity, and should not be treated as a lead.

admissions.text: 4,223 undergraduate students as of Fall 2024, a 47 percent four year graduation rate, and 74 percent of students receiving need based financial aid.

financial.text: S&P downgraded the school's long term credit rating from BBB minus to BB plus, which is below investment grade, in June 2025, on $154.5 million of debt, with a negative outlook. The school's operating deficit for the year was $17.1 million, and it broke a debt coverage agreement tied to a $132 million loan from 2019.

housing.text: We could not find this kind of enrollment data published anywhere on the university's website. Its own institutional data page only shows live dashboards and tells people to contact the office directly for more.

name: Southern New Hampshire University

financial.note: The only construction activity found is one small renovation; no loan or bond signal was found

demand.note: The physical campus is intentionally small; this is not a growth story on campus, even though the school's online enrollment nationally is very large

housing.note: This school has not published enrollment data of this kind anywhere we could find

flagNote: Included on purpose as the quiet case, to show this tool does not flag every school as exciting. The school's large online enrollment does not translate into on campus construction activity.

admissions.text: 2,615 students live and study on the physical campus as of Fall 2024, a small number compared to the school's very large national online enrollment.

financial.text: The only construction activity we found is a renovation of the Freese Student Center, with a contractor selected in October 2025. We did not find any loan, bond, or credit rating news for this school.

housing.text: We could not find this kind of enrollment data published anywhere on the university's website. Its consumer information page does not mention one, and we found nothing in library or records archives either.
